messages.author: 27405c4b711a1080
messages.subject: Defining relative binning for stat_bin/geom_histogram
parts:
Using an example from the geom_histogram page...

ggplot(data=movies, aes(rating))+ geom_histogram()
#stat_bin: binwidth defaulted to range/30. Use 'binwidth = x' to adjust this.

Say I wanted to define the bins at range/40 or range/50. 

> ggplot(data=movies, aes(rating))+ geom_histogram(binwidth=range/50)
Error in range/50 : non-numeric argument to binary operator

Putting it in as such doesn't work, which makes sense since "range" isn't a define variable... is there a shortcut call or do I have to calculate it on the fly?


I'm making graphs in a loop and there are many variables with varying data ranges that I would like with similar bins. If I don't have to calculate it it would be a lot easier. 

Brandon

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: Defining relative binning for stat_bin/geom_histogram
parts:
Hi Brandon:

Ratings only go from 1 to 10 :)

Here's one way, a little more generic:
> x <- diff(range(movies$rating))
> x
[1] 9
> ggplot(data=movies, aes(rating))+ geom_histogram(binwidth=I(x/50))
# or
> ggplot(data=movies, aes(rating))+ geom_histogram(binwidth=x/50)

Both work for me. binwidth =  needs a value as input.

HTH,
Dennis

messages.subject: Re: Defining relative binning for stat_bin/geom_histogram
parts:
On this topic,

One thing I've often wondered, but assumed the answer was no, was
whether it's possible to do this generally in the context of a faceted
plot. So... using Brandon's syntactical example:

ggplot(data=movies, aes(rating)) + geom_histogram(binwidth=range/50) +
facet_wrap(~othervariable, scales='free')

Obviously on some data set other than movies$rating, where the range
might vary greatly depending on the othervariable. Probably not,
right?

-danny
